Verified the design's own claim that mounting is already done as a REQ-070 side effect, that its AC-count correction (7 vs the Step 00 handoff's paraphrased 6) is accurate, that no implementation code is present beyond illustrative ExUnit specs, that Tests 3 and 5 are technically sound, and that the AC2/AC4-GET stub-router findings are genuine rather than a scope dodge.

result.summary:
PASS. Read docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-071 entry directly (awk range REQ-071..REQ-072): confirms 7 acceptance_criteria items verbatim, matching the design doc's Section 1a correction exactly (AC4 migrating-POST/GET-200 pair and AC5 concurrent-isolation are indeed two separate list items, not one) -- the design's claimed discrepancy against this run's own Step 00 handoff paraphrase is real, not fabricated. Section 8's traceability table maps all 7 ACs to concrete design elements (Section 1's structural verification + Section 3's 5 test specs + Section 2's moduledoc text + Section 4's REVIEWER-check pointer); no AC dropped or merged.

Read lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex, auth_pipeline.ex, tenant_status.ex, and router.ex directly: confirmed api_pipeline.ex:28-29 mounts AuthPipeline then TenantStatus immediately after Plug.Parsers (line 27) and before :match/:dispatch (30-31), exactly as the design states; router.ex declares GET /health before the /api/v1 forward, matching Section 1 AC3's claim; tenant_status.ex:58-59's Repo.get(Tenant, tenant_id) has no try/rescue/with anywhere in the module, confirming Section 1 AC5's fail-closed claim is real. Read lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex directly: confirmed it is a genuine stub (single match _ -> Letflow.Api.Response.not_found(conn) clause), so the design's AC2/AC4-GET findings (no route exists that can honestly return a literal 200/reach a real handler) are verified true, not an excuse -- both are reported as MINOR issues in the Step 01 handoff, consistent with 'no issue left local-only'.

Spot-checked the two riskiest test specs directly against source and existing test-file precedent rather than trusting the design's prose: (1) Tenant's schema (lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex:52) declares @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true} -- Repo.get(Tenant, "not-a-uuid") does raise Ecto.Query.CastError when the id argument fails to cast to :binary_id, confirming Test 5's assertion is technically correct. (2) Test 5's Task.async concurrency claim: read test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs:74-112 directly, which shows insert_tenant_for_realm!/1 (the exact helper Test 5 reuses) switches Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox to global :auto mode BEFORE inserting the tenant row, and stays in that mode for the rest of the test -- so by the time Test 5's Task.async calls run, the Repo is in :auto (real-pool, no per-process checkout) mode, not :manual/:shared mode. The well-known 'Task needs Sandbox.allow/3' gotcha applies only to :manual/:shared mode; it does not apply here because insert_tenant_for_realm!/1 already switched modes synchronously before the tasks were spawned. Verified this is not merely asserted by the design but independently reproducible from the cited precedent file's own code and comments (lines 74-89 explain exactly why :auto is required: Ecto.Migrator cannot run under the sandbox's shared single connection).

One MINOR non-blocking gap noted but not sufficient for FAIL: the design does not explicitly mandate async: false for the new test/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline_integration_test.exs module, even though its own cited precedent (auth_pipeline_test.exs:45) states its module is async: false specifically because of the same :auto-mode switch, and a global :auto switch is unsafe to run concurrently with other async modules' :shared-mode checkouts. This is a real ambiguity CODE-DESIGNER left unstated, but ExUnit.Case defaults a module to non-async when no :async option is given at all, which happens to produce the safe outcome even without an explicit instruction. This does not rise to a build-blocking ambiguity (TEST-DESIGNER inherits the safe default by omission, matching every other :auto-mode file in this codebase), so it is recorded here as a note for TEST-DESIGNER/TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to confirm explicitly (mirroring the design's own Section 7 OQ-1 treatment of Test 3's async setting) rather than a FAIL condition.

Confirmed no implementation code is present: all three code-fenced blocks in Section 3 are ExUnit test-spec sketches (describe/test blocks using conn/2, Task.async, assert), which is CODE-DESIGNER's charter-permitted test-specification convention, not production lib/ code; Section 2's moduledoc replacement text is prose, not compiled code; Section 4 quotes 2 lines of *existing* shipped code for REVIEWER to verify, not new code to write. Grepped Section 2/3/4 for defmodule/def outside quoted moduledoc/existing-code blocks -- none found introducing new production logic.

Confirmed docs/migration/stage-4-api-surface.md's REVIEWER sign-off section (read directly, lines 221+) already holds exactly the REQ-065 and REQ-084 PASS entries the design describes, in the same prose-plus-bullets format Section 4 asks the REQ-071 entry to follow -- insertion-point claim verified accurate.

Open questions (Section 7) are genuinely open (Test 3's async setting, whether AC2/AC4-GET's yaml wording itself should be corrected, telemetry-helper style) -- none of these represent a decision the design should have made itself; all three are legitimately cross-cutting calls for ORCH/TEST-DESIGNER/REVIEWER, not disguised avoidance.

Design is unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to apply the two moduledoc replacements verbatim and for TEST-DESIGNER to implement all 5 test specs without inventing undocumented behavior.
